messages:
incident-bot: SEV-2 alert: cluster-east-1 p95 latency spike + spike in 503s for inference service. auto-assigning to rotation.

ariana (oncall): I see it, p95 jumped from 180ms -> 1.8s, error rate 503 up from 0.2% -> 4.6%. Notifying SRE. @devon can you triage?

devon (sre): on it. pulling metrics now. quick question — any config rollouts in the last 30m?

kai (eng-runtime): yes, we pushed a continuous-batching change ~22m ago. increased max_num_seqs from 64 -> 256 and max_batch_tokens from 64k -> 256k for higher throughput on long-chat workloads. We thought it would help, but may be overloading KV cache.

maria (eng-ml): hmm that explains the memory graph. seeing steady growth in GPU-side KV cache residency and then sudden evictions. paging metrics show heavy host memory pressure -> swap churn on some nodes.

ariana (oncall): customers impacted? luis, can you surface top 5 customers hit and severity?

luis (customer-obs): yes — 3 customers show sustained 5-10x tail latency and some 50% increase in retries. One enterprise (acct-452) reported timeouts in their webhook flow. Opening customer thread.

devon (sre): root-cause hypothesis: batching params too aggressive -> massive multi-seq batches allocate huge KV pages -> eviction + host paging -> stalls -> timeouts. Also saw continuous-batch timeouts occuring more frequently (timeouts/sec spike).

sam (prodops): can we rollback the batch rollout? last deployment id is deploy-20280324-1322. If runtime config is feature-flagged we can flip it.

kai (eng-runtime): config is roll-forwardable via feature flag `cont_batch_params_v2`. Patching that is fastest. Recommend: 1) immediate rollback of params to previous stable values 2) reduce max_batch_tokens 3) lower max_num_seqs 4) enable aggressive kv eviction TTL.

ariana (oncall): do it. devon/sam coordinate rollback. kai provide exact config patch.

kai (eng-runtime): applying patch now. patch snippet: ```json
{
  "cont_batch_params": {
    "max_num_seqs": 64,
    "max_batch_tokens": 65536,
    "batch_timeout_ms": 30,
    "enable_prefetch": false
  }
}
```

incident-bot: change requested by kai applied to 3/5 runtime pools (canary first). patch-id: patch-2082109876-a.

devon (sre): verifying metrics. watching p95 and swap-in rates. canary nodes look stable. no more swap churn on canary.

maria (eng-ml): KV cache hit-rate decreased briefly (evictions) but overall stability improved. paging IO down to baseline.

ariana (oncall): proceed with gradual rollout to remaining pools with 30s pauses between rings. sam, coordinate with infra for restart windows.

sam (prodops): rolling now. ring-2 -> ring-3 -> ring-4. will notify if any anomalies.

support-bot: customer notifications queued for acct-452 and acct-781, draft message: "We're investigating an intermittent timeout impacting inference calls. We're applying a fix and will follow up."

luis (customer-obs): forwarded to PMs and AMs. customers appreciate rapid mitigation.

devon (sre): monitoring shows p95 back to ~220ms across clusters, 503s back to 0.4%. still watching for residual errors.

kai (eng-runtime): quick postmortem notes: the aggregation of max_num_seqs=256 + max_batch_tokens=256k allowed pathological batch constructions when many medium-length sequences aligned, producing very large KV footprints. Under memory pressure the eviction policy interacts poorly with our host-level OOM avoidance causing swap storms. We'll add a protective guard: a per-request max_kv_memory cap and a soft limiter that rejects creating batches > X tokens.

maria (eng-ml): also adding regression test to the CI eval harness to simulate aligned-seq workloads and measure KV memory delta.

ariana (oncall): moving to monitoring phase. next steps for oncall handoff: I'll update the incident ticket with timeline and hand to next rotation in 2 hours. Please add action items.

devon (sre): action items: - revert cont_batch_params in runtime config (done) - add per-pool kv_memory_limit (P1) - add alert for swap-in-rate > 0.5/s per node (P2) - schedule postmortem (P3)

kai (eng-runtime): creating a short hotfix for the config service: will add code to cap max_batch_tokens at 128k when max_num_seqs > 128. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/8421

sam (prodops): rollout completed to all rings at +14m. no further regressions observed.

incident-bot: SEV-2 -> SEV-3 downgraded. no active customer-facing impact.

ariana (oncall): handing off to @devon for post-incident follow-ups. next rotation please review the PR and confirm regression test coverage.

devon (sre): acknowledged. I'll schedule the postmortem and ping eng-runtime and eng-ml. assigning owners: kai (runtime fixes), maria (eval/tests), sam (rollout docs).

maria (eng-ml): initial RCA note: miscalibrated scale for long-chat throughput. will propose new default of max_num_seqs=96 and max_batch_tokens=96k for multi-tenant clusters.

luis (customer-obs): customer status: all impacted customers contacted; two asked for root cause — we'll share postmortem draft after internal review.

ariana (oncall): adding timeline to incident ticket: 00:00 alert, +02m assign, +10m identified config rollout, +22m rollback started, +36m stable. close once postmortem and PR merged.

pagerduty-bot: Incident 2082109876 updated: status -> monitoring.

support-bot: follow-up draft saved to docs/incidents/2082109876-cust-mail.md

devon (sre): quick note — we should also check edge-case timeouts: batch_timeout_ms lowered from 100 -> 30 in patch. we need to validate it doesn't increase small-request latency. adding short perf run.

kai (eng-runtime): agreed. running synthetic load test against staging with a mix of short and long sessions. results wil be attached to PR.

ariana (oncall): thanks team. devon, please take the incident to postmortem. I'll mark the channel as resolved in 1h if no new anomalies. :white_check_mark:
